_meanings:
.²1 A carpenter, builder, workman, {#tvazwreva vihitaM yantram#} <ls>Mb. 12. 33. 22</ls>.
.²2 Viśvakarman, the architect of the gods. [Tvaṣtṛ is the Vulcan of
 the Hindu mythology. He had a son named Triśiras and a daughter called
 {#saMjYA#}, who was given in marriage to the sun. But she was unable to
 bear the severe light of her husband, and therefore Tvaṣtṛ mounted
 the sun upon his lathe, and carefully trimmed off a part of his bright
 disc; <ab>cf.</ab> {#Aropya cakraBramimuzRatejAstvazwreva yatnolliKito viBAti#}
 <ls>R. 6. 32</ls>. The part trimmed off is said to have been used by him in forming
 the discus of Viṣṇu, the Triśūla of Śiva, and some other weapons
 of the gods.] {#parvataM cApi jagrAha krudDastvazwA mahAbalaH#} <ls>Mb. 1. 227. 34</ls>.
.²3 Prajāpati (the creator); {#yAM cakAra svayaM tvazwA rAmasya mahizIM#}
 {#priyAm#} <ls>Mb. 3. 274. 9</ls>.
.²4 Āditya, a form of the sun; {#nirBinne akziRI tvazwA lokapAlo'viSadviBoH#}
 <ls>Bhāg. 3. 6. 15</ls>.
